segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Hey Chris, do you have two minutes on the Northstar renewal? They're trying to get the order form today for a February 1 go-live on the extra teams.

segments.speaker: Chris
segments.text: Yeah, I've got it open in the CRM. Current is 84 seats at $38,640 annually, and you're adding 36 seats, right?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Correct, 120 total. They also want the reporting add-on for just the admin group, so 12 users. Pricing sheet shows $18 per admin per month.

segments.speaker: Chris
segments.text: Okay, so net new is 36 seats at the blended rate plus $2,592 for reporting. With the midterm co-term to October 31, the order form should land at $13,744. Does that match what you quoted?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, I quoted $13,700-ish, so that's fine. The only issue is I've nudged legal and finance a few times on the billing clause they asked for, and the deal's basically sitting until that sign-off comes back.

segments.speaker: Chris
segments.text: Got it. Is that the clause about invoicing the expansion on March 15 instead of at signature?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Exactly. Their AP team only runs vendor payments twice a month, and procurement won't approve if the invoice date says due on receipt.

segments.speaker: Chris
segments.text: Okay, I can draft the order form with the standard net 30 language and leave the invoice date field blank for now. Once they clear it, I can push it through deal desk.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: That works. Also, no discount beyond what they already have. VP asked, but they accepted the current 8% if we hold the October renewal date.

segments.speaker: Chris
segments.text: Perfect. Send me the email thread with procurement, and I'll update the billing tool notes so there isn't a mismatch when finance generates the invoice.
